section_summary: This section contains German press translations on Japan’s 1944–45 budget, wartime savings, and paper currency, followed by State Department records on Japanese dollar bonds and bank transactions. Most of the section is a draft manual for the financial and accounting work of U.S. civil affairs forces operating in Japan.

people.name: Williams
people.role: State Department adviser on Japanese financial and economic matters

people.name: James C. Dunn
people.role: Adviser on Political Relations; Director, Office of European Affairs

people.name: A. H. Carter
people.role: Major General and Fiscal Director, Army Service Forces

people.name: Dooman
people.role: Division of Far Eastern Affairs official

subfiles.title: Japanese Circulation of Paper Currency
subfiles.about: Reports rising banknote circulation in Japan, Korea, and Formosa.
subfiles.summary: The Finance Minister attributes increased currency circulation to business funding, cash use, and wartime industrial growth.

subfiles.title: Japanese Savings
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese Finance Minister’s savings estimates for fiscal 1944–45.
subfiles.summary: Projected national income is 60 billion yen, with 36 billion yen expected in savings.

subfiles.title: Japanese Budget for 1944–45 and Circulation of Paper Currency
subfiles.from: J. Klahr Huddle, American Legation, Bern
subfiles.about: Transmits three German press translations on Japan’s budget, currency, and savings.
subfiles.summary: Huddle supplements earlier budget reporting with the attached translations.

subfiles.title: Japanese Special Budget Estimates for the Conduct of the War
subfiles.about: Details Japan’s proposed special war budget and borrowing requirements.
subfiles.summary: The proposed war budget totals 38 billion yen, including 20.8 billion in government loans.

subfiles.title: Japanese Circulation of Paper Currency
subfiles.about: Repeats the report on increased banknote circulation in Japan, Korea, and Formosa.
subfiles.summary: Rising currency issues are linked to cash transactions, employment, wages, and war production.

subfiles.title: Japanese Savings
subfiles.about: Repeats the Finance Minister’s fiscal 1944–45 savings projections.
subfiles.summary: Projected savings would finance government and industrial requirements after taxes.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Routing Sheet
subfiles.about: Records internal routing of the Japanese budget material.
subfiles.summary: Mostly illegible routing marks.

subfiles.title: Japanese Budget for Fiscal Year 1944–1945
subfiles.from: J. Klahr Huddle, American Legation, Bern
subfiles.about: Forwards a German article summarizing Japan’s 1944–45 budget.
subfiles.summary: The enclosed article was dated at Yokohama in mid-December 1943.

subfiles.title: Further Adaptation of Japanese Business to Total War
subfiles.about: Describes wartime economic reorganization and Japan’s proposed 1944–45 budget.
subfiles.summary: The article portrays the ordinary budget as devoted largely to war production. It lists ministry appropriations, new spending, tax increases, and government borrowing, and estimates that the ordinary and special war budgets together may reach 50 billion yen.

subfiles.title: Possible Repatriation of Japanese Dollar Bonds
subfiles.about: Assesses a proposed negotiation concerning Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The writer considers a $20 million opening proposal too low, reviews outstanding bonds and U.S. holdings, and recommends a higher initial valuation to allow bargaining.

subfiles.title: Japanese Dollar Bonds
subfiles.about: Relays Securities and Exchange Commission advice on trading and repurchasing Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Japanese bonds had been removed from exchanges after Pearl Harbor. Lauchheim warns that a Treasury purchase offer could create a speculative market and objections from bondholders, while offering SEC assistance if the departments proceed.

subfiles.title: Japanese Financial and Economic Conditions
subfiles.about: Points to a military attaché report of a conversation with two Russian couriers.
subfiles.summary: Directs readers to the original report in file 894.50.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government Bonds at the Yokohama Specie Bank
subfiles.about: Reports FBI information on Japanese government bonds found in San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Investigators found $5,554,900 in bonds concealed at the bank, apparently intended for secret shipment aboard a Japanese vessel. Another $1,737,000 shipment from New York was reportedly impounded; examiners were checking the bank’s claim that the concealed bonds had been canceled.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Specie Bank Withdrawals
subfiles.about: Reports FBI information on cash withdrawals and transfers by the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: The bank withdrew cash in New York and transferred $1.39 million to San Francisco and Seattle banks.

subfiles.title: Comment on Manual of Financial and Accounting Procedures
subfiles.about: Conveys State Department concurrence with the draft manual for use in Japan.
subfiles.summary: State Department officers found no provision impracticable and suggested no changes.

subfiles.title: Request to Prepare Reply on Financial Procedures Manual
subfiles.about: Requests a letter responding to General Carter’s draft manual.
subfiles.summary: Labouisse forwards Dooman’s note and asks Reinstein to prepare Dunn’s reply.

subfiles.title: Review of Financial Procedures Manual
subfiles.about: Reports Far Eastern Affairs’ review of the draft manual.
subfiles.summary: Dooman concurs with Williams that the procedures appear practicable, though they require extensive paperwork.

subfiles.title: Request for Views on Financial Procedures Manual
subfiles.about: Seeks comments on the draft manual for civil affairs forces in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Labouisse sends Dooman a copy and notes that Reinstein also received one.

subfiles.title: Submission of Draft Manual of Financial and Accounting Procedures
subfiles.about: Submits two draft copies of the manual for comment or concurrence.
subfiles.summary: The manual is intended for U.S. civil affairs forces operating in Japan proper, excluding Formosa.

subfiles.title: Confidential Cover
subfiles.about: Marks the enclosed manual as confidential.
subfiles.summary: Confidential classification cover.

subfiles.title: Draft Manual of Financial and Accounting Procedures
subfiles.from: War Department, in collaboration with Navy Department
subfiles.to: Financial Divisions of Civil Affairs Sections
subfiles.about: Sets out proposed financial controls and accounting procedures for U.S. civil affairs operations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The foreword describes the manual as guidance for commanders planning financial administration in Japan proper, except Formosa. Its organization chart assigns responsibilities for government agencies, financial institutions, commerce, funds control, accounts, and audit. The chapters in this section prescribe custody and transfer of funds, disbursing and revenue collection records, revolving funds, monthly reports, officer handovers, field supervision, and the approval of advances to governmental agencies. The manual continues beyond page 320.
